Subject: DTIA evidence and sandbox/proxy routing clarifications

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the quick call earlier. Legal have asked for a concise packet we can review for our internal DTIA (data transfer impact assessment) — specifically we need:

- A completed DTIA questionnaire (I attached our template).
- Clear statements on where tokenized data might cross borders (edge vs core).
- Any existing bridge-letter or UK IDTA/UK Addendum related language you rely on.
- A list of subprocessors that may process telemetry or KV cache replicas (and whether they are EU-hosted).

Two follow-ups from our infra team: they want to understand whether Redwood can run an isolated sandbox/proxy pattern where EU-origin traffic is routed through an onshore proxy (short-term) and whether there is a documented failover to hosted global pools. Any diagrams or timelines are helpful.

We'd like to share the packet with our DPO on Monday. Can you get the DTIA checklist and a short description of the proxy/sandbox approach over by EOD Friday (your timezone)?

Thanks,
Marta

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the note. We're assembling a focused packet for you. High level:

- DTIA questionnaire: completed answers (working draft) attached.
- Cross-border flows: by default our hosted runtime may replicate short-lived KV data for caching to accelerate latency; we can configure EU-only routing for your account and pin models to EU regions.
- Subprocessors: included in the attachment (we list roles and hosting regions).
- Sandbox/proxy: Jordan will include a short diagram and the operational steps to create a temporary EU-side proxy (recommended for proof-of-concept) that pins requests to EU-dedicated pools and uses onshore cache w/ no offload to global pools.

Kimberly — can you review the attached bridge-letter draft and add any legal nuance re: UK addendum vs SCC reliance?

We'll get a single ZIP-ready packet by Friday EOD. If Monday DPO review is the deadline, we should be fine.

Action items I will own: packaging, a one-page summary, and a timeline for establishing the sandbox proxy.

Marcus / Marta —

I've reviewed Marcus's draft and made targeted edits to the bridge-letter language. Key points for EdgeHealth to note:

- Legal basis: For EU customers we propose primary reliance on SCCs (EU standard clauses) and then operationalize restricted routing as a contractual technical measure; where UK residency is required, the UK IDTA addendum will be referenced — we avoid promising structural guarantees that conflict with our fallback routing.
- Bridge letter: acceptable for transient caching replication where data is encrypted in transit and at rest, with a TTL under 24 hours for cached KV entries — this prevents long-term cross-border persistence.
- Subprocessors: we enumerate subprocessors and mark which have EU region hosting. We will provide SOC-2 scope and key-control attestations where available.
- Evidence: we can provide: signed bridge-letter draft (attached), a subprocessors table, and a concise infra diagram of the sandbox proxy.

Open question for infra: can we commit to a documented TTL enforcement for KV caches (24 hours)? Jordan, please confirm implementability and any caveats (cache warming, cold-start latency implications).

Marta — I'll also attach a redline of the bridge letter so you and your DPO can see the exact wording.

Regards,
Kimberly

Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 17:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DTIA evidence and sandbox/proxy routing clarifications

Kimberly / Marcus / Marta —

Quick infra confirmation and technical note:

- TTL enforcement: we can implement a hard TTL at the cache layer (configurable per-customer) and enforce eviction at 24h. Edge cases: short-lived prefetching (cache warming) may briefly create entries but these are still subject to the same TTL policy.
- Proxy/sandbox design: recommended pattern for proof-of-concept:
  1) Create an EU-dedicated proxy endpoint in your VPC/VNet (we support private endpoints).
  2) Route EU-origin client traffic to the proxy which pins to EU model pool and EU-only KV cache nodes.
  3) Use encrypted links (mTLS) to our EU control plane; no data egress to global pools unless explicit failover is triggered.
  4) Failover behavior: if EU pool capacity exhausted, requests hit a queued fallback that invokes onshore cache-first policy; automatic fallback to global pools only with documented escalation and an opt-in flag — we can disable global fallback entirely for initial pilot.
- Operational notes: there is measurable cold-start latency when pinning to single-region pools — estimate +80–150ms median for model spin-up vs multi-region burst. We'll provide baseline numbers from our perf tests.

Attachments: infra_proxy_diagram.png (simple diagram), and I included a short ops checklist in the packet Marcus is assembling.

Happy to run a 30-min tech walkthrough next week with EdgeHealth infra if that helps the DPO and engineering team.

-Jordan
